# Procurement Approval Matrix

## 1. Purpose

This matrix defines who may approve a purchase and what evidence is required at each value. It applies to goods and services bought from third parties, including software subscriptions, hardware, professional services and events. It does not apply to travel, which follows Finance_Travel_And_Expense_Policy, or to employee expenses, which follow Finance_Expense_Card_Policy.

## 2. Approval thresholds

| Purchase value (INR) | Approver | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 50,000 | Manager | Quote or price confirmation |
| 50,001 to 5,00,000 | Director | Two quotes, business justification |
| Above 5,00,000 | CFO | Three quotes, business case, budget confirmation |

Thresholds apply to the total contract value, not to the annual or monthly instalment. A three-year contract at INR 2,00,000 per year is a INR 6,00,000 purchase and needs CFO approval.

## 3. Quotes and competitive process

1. Purchases above INR 2,00,000 require at least three written quotes unless the vendor is sole-source.
2. Sole-source purchases require a written justification approved by the CFO.
3. Renewals of existing software may use the incumbent's quote if the price increase is below 7%; above that, the purchase is re-competed.
4. Quotes must be dated within 60 days of the approval request.

## 4. Purchase orders

2. Vendors must not start work before the purchase order is issued.

4. The purchase order must reference the budget line in Finance_Quarterly_Budget_Allocation.

# Capital Expenditure Policy

## 1. Definition

A purchase is capital expenditure when it costs more than INR 10,00,000 and provides benefit for more than 12 months. Below that threshold the purchase is expensed in the quarter it is incurred, even if it is hardware. Software subscriptions are expensed unless the contract grants a perpetual licence, in which case the licence fee is capitalised and the support element is expensed.

## 2. Approval

1. Capex requires a business case covering the problem, the options considered, the total cost of ownership, the payback period and the risk of not proceeding.
2. A payback period longer than 24 months requires the CFO's approval; longer than 36 months requires board approval.
3. Every capex request must name the budget line in Finance_Quarterly_Budget_Allocation.
4. Capex above INR 50,00,000 is reviewed by the investment committee, which meets monthly.

## 3. Capitalisation and depreciation

| Asset class | Useful life | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Computer hardware | 3 years | Straight line |
| Network equipment | 5 years | Straight line |
| Furniture and fixtures | 7 years | Straight line |
| Perpetual software licences | 3 years | Straight line |
| Leasehold improvements | Shorter of lease or 5 years | Straight line |

Depreciation starts in the month the asset is available for use, not the month it is paid for. Assets not yet in use are held as capital work in progress and reviewed each quarter.

## 4. Impairment

Assets are reviewed for impairment annually or when there is an indicator such as a product being discontinued. An impairment loss is recognised in the quarter it is identified and reported to the CFO.

## 5. Disposal

1. Disposal requires the asset owner's request and Finance approval.
2. Proceeds are recorded against the asset's net book value; any gain or loss is recognised in the income statement.
3. Data-bearing assets must be wiped under IT_Data_Classification_Standard before disposal, with a certificate retained.
4. Disposals above INR 5,00,000 are reported to the audit committee.

## 6. Leases

Leases longer than 12 months are recognised on the balance sheet in line with the applicable accounting standard. The facilities team maintains the lease register and provides it to Finance quarterly.

# Corporate Expense Card Policy

## 1. Eligibility

Corporate expense cards are issued to employees who travel at least once a quarter, to managers who buy team supplies, and to roles that purchase on behalf of the company. Cards are issued in the employee's name and remain company property. A card is cancelled on the last working day, and any balance is recovered from the final settlement if unaccounted.

## 2. Limits

1. The standard monthly limit is INR 1,00,000.
2. Directors and above have a monthly limit of INR 3,00,000.
3. Single-transaction limits are INR 25,000 for the standard card and INR 1,00,000 for the Director card.
4. Cash withdrawals are disabled.
5. Limits are reviewed annually and may be reduced after two consecutive late submissions.

## 3. Permitted spend

Travel bookings made through the corporate tool, meals within per diem, ground transport, team supplies approved by the manager, and software under INR 25,000 that is on the approved list. All spend must have a business purpose recorded at submission.

## 4. Prohibited spend

1. Personal purchases of any kind, even if reimbursed later.
2. Alcohol, entertainment and gifts, except as permitted by Legal_Anti_Corruption_Compliance.
3. Cash advances or person-to-person transfers.
4. Subscriptions that auto-renew without a purchase order.
5. Spend on behalf of another employee who has their own card.

1. Receipts must be uploaded within 7 days of the transaction.
2. Transactions without a receipt after 7 days are flagged to the manager; after 21 days they are recovered from salary.

4. Missing receipts for transactions under INR 500 may be replaced by a written declaration, limited to three per quarter.

# Vendor Security Review

## 1. When a review is required

Any third party that will store, process or access Meridian data must pass a security review before a contract is signed. This includes SaaS tools, contractors with system access, managed services and data processors. A review is not required for vendors that receive only Public information, but the classification must be recorded.

## 2. Process and timelines

1. The business owner submits the vendor request with the intended data classification and integration scope.
2. Security Engineering sends the standard questionnaire within 2 working days.
3. The vendor returns the questionnaire and evidence. The review concludes within 30 days of receiving complete evidence.
4. Reviews requiring a penetration test summary or a Data Processing Agreement take up to 45 days.
5. Contracts must not be signed before the review is recorded as passed.

## 3. Evidence requirements

1. SOC 2 Type II is required for any vendor processing Confidential or Restricted data. A SOC 2 Type I is accepted only with a remediation plan and a follow-up date.
2. ISO 27001 certification is accepted in place of SOC 2 where the scope covers the service in question.
3. Vendors without either certification require a documented compensating review by Security Engineering and approval from the CTO.
4. Encryption at rest and in transit must be evidenced.
5. Sub-processors must be listed and approved; unreported sub-processors are a contractual breach.

## 4. Data processing terms

Where personal data is involved, Legal_Data_Privacy_GDPR_Compliance requires a Data Processing Agreement. The DPA must cover purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, deletion on termination and audit rights. Vendors that cannot accept the standard terms are escalated to Legal.

## 5. Ongoing monitoring

1. Confidential and Restricted vendors are reassessed annually.
2. A vendor security incident must be reported to Meridian within 72 hours under the DPA.
3. Access granted to vendor staff is reviewed quarterly with the vendor's named contacts.
4. Vendors that fail two consecutive reassessments are placed on a remediation plan and may be terminated by the business owner.

## 6. Exceptions

An exception requires the CTO's written approval, a compensating control and an expiry date no later than 90 days. Exceptions are reported to the security committee monthly.

# Contract Review Process

## 1. Scope

This process covers every agreement Meridian signs with a third party: customer contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, data processing agreements, leases and statements of work. Employment contracts are handled by People Operations and are not reviewed here.

## 2. Service levels

1. Standard contract review takes 7 business days from receipt of a complete request.
2. Expedited review takes 48 hours and requires the department head to state the business reason.
3. NDAs on the approved template are reviewed within 1 business day.
4. A request without the counterparty's full draft, the deal summary and the commercial terms is not considered received.

## 3. Request requirements

1. Submit through the legal request system, not by email.
2. Include the counterparty name, the contract value, the term, the data involved and the business owner.
3. Attach the counterparty's draft and any redlines already exchanged.
4. State the deadline and the consequence of missing it.

## 4. Review standards

Legal reviews liability caps, indemnities, termination rights, data protection, payment terms, governing law and intellectual property. Any clause that deviates from the playbook requires a documented approval from the Head of Legal. Unlimited liability, most-favoured-nation pricing and exclusivity are escalation triggers.

## 5. Signature authority

1. Contracts up to INR 5,00,000 may be signed by a Director.
2. Contracts up to INR 50,00,000 require the CFO.
3. Contracts above INR 50,00,000 require the CEO.
4. Delegation must be in writing and is recorded in the authority register.

## 6. Post-signature

1. The executed contract is stored in the contract repository within 2 business days.
2. Finance is notified so payment terms and revenue schedules are set up.
3. Renewal alerts are set 90 days before expiry for contracts with auto-renewal.
4. Amendments follow the same review process as the original contract.

# Vendor Payment Terms

## 1. Default terms

1. The default payment term for vendor invoices is Net 45 from the invoice date.
2. The invoice date is the date the invoice is issued, not the date it is received.
3. Payment runs happen twice a month, on the 10th and the 25th. An invoice falling due between runs is paid on the next run.
4. Vendors must quote a purchase order number on every invoice; invoices without one are returned unpaid.

## 2. Early payment discount

1. Where a vendor offers a 2% discount for payment within 10 days, Accounts Payable takes the discount if the cash position allows.
2. The discount is calculated on the invoice value excluding taxes.
3. Discounts are recorded as a separate line in the vendor ledger, not netted against the payable.
4. Vendors offering a discount for payment within 5 days are reviewed by the treasury team before acceptance.

## 3. Invoice validation

1. A three-way match is required: purchase order, goods receipt and invoice.
2. Mismatches are resolved with the business owner within 5 working days.
3. Invoices above INR 10,00,000 require a second Finance review.
4. Duplicate invoices are flagged by the vendor ledger and are never paid twice.

## 4. Late payment

1. Interest is payable on late invoices at 1% per month where the delay exceeds 30 days beyond the agreed term.
2. Interest is not payable where the delay is caused by a missing purchase order or a disputed invoice.
3. Persistent late payment is reported to the CFO monthly.

## 5. Small invoices

Invoices below INR 5,00,000 are settled on Net 30 rather than Net 45. This exception exists to reduce the administrative cost of low-value payables and does not require a contract amendment. Where a contract states Net 45 for a vendor whose invoices are consistently below the threshold, Accounts Payable applies Net 30 and records the deviation in the vendor file. Business owners should expect the shorter term when planning cash.

## 6. Foreign currency

Foreign currency invoices are paid in the invoice currency. The exchange rate is the bank rate on the payment date. Vendors may not require payment in a currency other than the contract currency.

- Finance_Procurement_Approval_Matrix for purchase orders.
- IT_Vendor_Security_Review for data-handling

# Procurement Approval Matrix

## 1. Purpose

This matrix defines who may approve a purchase and what evidence is required at each value. It applies to goods and services bought from third parties, including software subscriptions, hardware, professional services and events. It does not apply to travel, which follows Finance_Travel_And_Expense_Policy, or to employee expenses, which follow Finance_Expense_Card_Policy.

## 2. Approval thresholds

| Purchase value (INR) | Approver | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 50,000 | Manager | Quote or price confirmation |
| 50,001 to 5,00,000 | Director | Two quotes, business justification |
| Above 5,00,000 | CFO | Three quotes, business case, budget confirmation |

Thresholds apply to the total contract value, not to the annual or monthly instalment. A three-year contract at INR 2,00,000 per year is a INR 6,00,000 purchase and needs CFO approval.

1. Purchases above INR 2,00,000 require at least three written quotes unless the vendor is sole-source.
2. Sole-source purchases require a written justification approved by the CFO.
3. Renewals of existing software may use the incumbent's quote if the price increase is below 7%; above that, the purchase is re-competed.

# Contract Review Process

## 1. Scope

This process covers every agreement Meridian signs with a third party: customer contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, data processing agreements, leases and statements of work. Employment contracts are handled by People Operations and are not reviewed here.

## 2. Service levels

1. Standard contract review takes 7 business days from receipt of a complete request.
2. Expedited review takes 48 hours and requires the department head to state the business reason.
3. NDAs on the approved template are reviewed within 1 business day.
4. A request without the counterparty's full draft, the deal summary and the commercial terms is not considered received.

## 3. Request requirements

1. Submit through the legal request system, not by email.
2. Include the counterparty name, the contract value, the term, the data involved and the business owner.
3. Attach the counterparty's draft and any redlines already exchanged.
4. State the deadline and the consequence of missing it.

## 4. Review standards

Legal reviews liability caps, indemnities, termination rights, data protection, payment terms, governing law and intellectual property. Any clause that deviates from the playbook requires a documented approval from the Head of Legal. Unlimited liability, most-favoured-nation pricing and exclusivity are escalation triggers.

## 5. Signature authority

1. Contracts up to INR 5,00,000 may be signed by a Director.
2. Contracts up to INR 50,00,000 require the CFO.
3. Contracts above INR 50,00,000 require the CEO.
4. Delegation must be in writing and is recorded in the authority register.

## 6. Post-signature

1. The executed contract is stored in the contract repository within 2 business days.
2. Finance is notified so payment terms and revenue schedules are set up.
3. Renewal alerts are set 90 days before expiry for contracts with auto-renewal.
4. Amendments follow the same review process as the original contract.

Corporate expense cards are issued to employees who travel at least once a quarter, to managers who buy team supplies, and to roles that purchase on behalf of the company.
